title: Crypto Community Promo (Weight-Loss Testimonial Parody)
notes: Parody of the mother.satori clinic-interview format, two acts. STRUCTURE (2026-05-30): each act is a LOCKED STATIC TRIPOD framing — one camera, no moves, no angle changes, just watching the interview. The conversation plays out as a sequence of ~15s generations chained last-frame->first-frame; each generation animates ONE speaker while the other listens idle. SCENE 1 (s1-clinic) = the 'before' interview in a grimy WELLNESS CLINIC: Mike (mic, frame-right, standing) interviews a heavier-set woman (frame-left, seated). Six speaker-turns inside one held two-shot (see scene.turns). SCENE 2+ = '3 months later' at a LAVISH TROPICAL RESORT BAR (consolidated 2026-05-30 into ONE held two-shot with turns[], same as the clinic). Setting contrast (clinic->resort) sells the before/after. CHARACTERS: Mike (real refs in identity/); the WOMAN (fictional) needed in BOTH states (heavier 'before' + slim 'after') with her own soft feminine voice — still the gating asset; a brief slim FRIEND enters in s2i. Gaze cues are FRAME-RELATIVE (Seedance reads gaze from viewer POV). Specific calls (MYX 550x, De-Agent AI 130x, Pippin, Lab) and the CryptoRich.vip CTA are Mike's promo content — keep verbatim. Per-turn prompts pass VERBATIM to Seedance.

friend.look: younger attractive woman; enters in s2i only (single shot, low consistency need)

characters.tone: sex appeal + humor; parody of testimonial ads + crypto-bro culture; all characters clearly adults

You: "So, when did your husband stop touching you?"

You: "And what happened after that?"

scenes.prompt: A grimy, dimly lit wellness clinic. LOCKED STATIC TRIPOD TWO-SHOT, vertical 9:16, the camera does not move or change angle for the entire interview. A man with curly hair and glasses stands on the RIGHT of the frame holding a microphone; a heavier-set woman in a dirty white t-shirt and grey sweatpants sits on the LEFT. Dim flickering fluorescent light, run-down clinic background. The camera holds this exact framing while they take turns speaking — when one talks the other listens naturally (small head movements, blinking, breathing), never frozen.
